comment: SINGLE-FIELD COLLECTION-GROUP SCOPES GO IN fieldOverrides, NOT IN indexes.
The two public lookups below each need one field indexed across every
workspace. Both were declared as entries in `indexes` with a single field,
which Firestore rejects outright: 'this index is not necessary, configure
using single field index controls'. The whole file was therefore
undeployable — `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` failed before it
got to anything else, so no index work of any kind could ship.
They are declared as fieldOverrides instead, which is the supported way to
widen ONE field's scope to COLLECTION_GROUP, and which deploys from this
file like everything else. Nothing here is configured by hand in the
console: the repo stays the source of truth, and an exemption cannot be
deleted out from under the Cloud Functions without this file disagreeing.
EACH OVERRIDE ALSO RESTATES THE COLLECTION-SCOPED INDEXES. A fieldOverride
REPLACES Firestore's automatic single-field indexing for that field, so
listing only the COLLECTION_GROUP scope would quietly drop the ordinary
per-collection indexes the app's own queries use.
`indexes` is legitimately empty: the app has no composite indexes.
Composite ones belong there when they arrive.

fieldOverrides.comment: Public repair-status lookup (repairStatusLookup Cloud Function): collectionGroup('repairs').where('repairNumber','==',ticket) — an equality match across every workspace, so it needs the COLLECTION_GROUP scope below. Do not remove it; the public status page stops resolving ticket numbers without it.

Public PC-build listing lookup (buildShareLookup Cloud Function): collectionGroup('pcBuilds').where('shareToken','==',token) — the same shape. Do not remove it; every shared build link stops resolving without it.
